I also read three sibling files: Estimates/RestrictedNoStopParameters.lean, Angular/AngularRestrictedNoStopParameters.lean and Theta/CubicThetaCentralAngularRestrictedNoStopParameters.lean. I also checked the statements of restricted_noStop_central_bound_actual, restricted_noStop_central_bound, eventually_noStop_scales, primeProductWeights (whose index type is Unit) and angular_distinguishedScaleNoStop. Both proofs in the target are line-for-line copies of proofs elsewhere in the repository. The only differences are the upstream theorem invoked (the `_actual` version without hV, or the version with hV) and the angular parameter (0 or ℓ). The isLittleO proof appears four times, once in each of the four files. The patterson-bound proof appears twice. The two definitions distinguishedScaleNoStop and angular_distinguishedScaleNoStop have identical bodies except for the literal 0 versus ℓ. So a lemma stated with the sum written out, at a general ℓ, matches both after `unfold`. I could not run Lean, so the proposed rewrites are untested sketches. findings.benefit: About 45 lines of asymptotic bookkeeping repeated four times become one lemma with a descriptive statement. Each of the four isLittleO theorems shrinks to a short reduction to its patterson bound. That makes it clear that the theorems differ only in their upstream analytic input. A future change, such as a new exponent, cutoff or tuple count, then needs one edit instead of four synchronized edits.

findings.problem: The proof of restricted_noStop_patterson_bound_actual specializes the central bound at Z = X^(38/100) and Y = X^(2/5). It then discharges the six scale side conditions using the six components of eventually_noStop_scales, bounds 1+log(X^(2/5)) by 1+log X via Real.log_rpow, and finishes with gcongr and pow_succ. This same block is restricted_noStop_patterson_bound (Estimates/RestrictedNoStopParameters.lean, lines 30–45). The only difference is that it calls restricted_noStop_central_bound with hV instead of restricted_noStop_central_bound_actual. The two central-bound theorems have identical conclusions, and nothing after the `obtain` depends on which theorem produced `hbound`.

  ∀ᶠ X : ℝ in atTop, ∀ (i : γ) (R : Finset Eisenstein) (v : Eisenstein → ℂ) (P : Eisenstein → Eisenstein → Prop) (ψ : ℝ → ℝ) (w H X₀ : ℝ), 0 < H → (∀ r ∈ R, primary r) → (∀ r ∈ R, ‖v r‖ ≤ M) → (∀ x, 0 ≤ ψ x ∧ ψ x ≤ 1) → ‖restrictedNoStopCenteredValue R v ψ w ρ (X^(38/100:ℝ)) (Real.exp hW.radius) ℓ (W i) H ((1+Real.log X)^Ct) X X₀ P‖ ≤ K*(1+Real.log X)^(Ct+1)*X^(5/6-1/100:ℝ)
